1.title: Ingesting Data (1): Connectors, AMA, Data Collection Rules and Windows Events
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Ingesting Data (one): Connectors, A M A, Data Collection Rules and Windows Events. It covers the exam area one. Manage a security operations environment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Select data connectors based on data source requirements, including Windows logs and security events. Configure collection of Windows Security events by using Windows Security Events via A M A, including data collection rules. Plan and configure collection of Windows Security events by using Windows Event Forwarding (W E F). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one. Manage a security operations environment (forty to forty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: How data reaches Sentinel
1.text: How data reaches Sentinel. The figure shows this: Source, agent, data collection rule and workspace table.

1.title: How data reaches Sentinel, continued
1.text: How data reaches Sentinel. A data connector brings a source into a Log Analytics workspace table. Connectors come from Content hub solutions; you configure them under Microsoft Sentinel, then Configuration, then Data connectors. Service to service. Microsoft Defender X D R, Microsoft Entra I D, Office three sixty-five, Azure services. Agent-based (Azure Monitor Agent, A M A). Windows Security Events via A M A, Windows Forwarded Events, sys log via A M A, C E F via A M A. Diagnostic settings or Azure Policy. Azure Activity, Azure resources. A P I or file. Logs Ingestion A P I, threat intelligence upload, taxi.

1.title: How data reaches Sentinel, continued
1.text: How data reaches Sentinel. The Azure Monitor Agent (A M A) replaces the legacy Log Analytics agent. A data collection rule (D C R) tells A M A what to collect, can filter or transform it, and names the destination workspace. Deploy the agent. Virtual Machine Contributor or Azure Connected Machine Resource Administrator. Create or edit D C Rs. Monitoring Contributor. Configure a connector. Read and write on the Sentinel workspace. Exam tip: A M A plus D C R is the modern pattern. Machines outside Azure (on-premises or other clouds) need Azure Arc first, so that A M A can be installed.

1.title: Windows Security Events via AMA
1.text: Windows Security Events via A M A. Table: Security Event. On the connector page choose Create data collection rule, select the machines, then choose what to collect on the Collect tab. All events. Every Windows security event. Common. A standard set for security analysis. Minimal. A small set (sign-in and a few key events). Custom. Only the events matched by X path queries you write.

1.title: Windows Security Events via AMA, continued
1.text: Windows Security Events via A M A. Version. A M A supports X path one point zero only. Limits. Up to twenty expressions per box and one hundred boxes per rule. Example. Security! System Event I D four thousand six hundred twenty-four or Event I D four thousand six hundred twenty-five (successful and failed logons). Validate. Get-Win Event -Filter XPath on a test machine. Exam tip: Custom equals X path. To collect only logons and logoffs, write an X path on the Security log with the event I D s; do not collect All events, because that costs more.

1.title: Windows Forwarded Events and WEF
1.text: Windows Forwarded Events and W E F. Windows Event Forwarding (W E F) sends events from many source computers to one Windows Event Collector (W E C) server over Win R M. Sentinel then reads the Forwarded Events log on the collector. This is useful when sources cannot run an agent. Connector. Windows Forwarded Events via A M A. Install A M A on. The W E C machine, not on every source. Prerequisite. Windows Event Collection enabled and running on the collector. Table. Windows Event (not Security Event), even for events forwarded from the Security log. Built-in rules. Rules that query Security Event need the Windows Security Events via A M A connector.

1.title: Windows Forwarded Events and WEF, continued
1.text: Windows Forwarded Events and W E F. Source-initiated. Sources are pointed to the collector by Group Policy; scales to many computers. Collector-initiated. The collector pulls from a fixed list of sources. Plan the W E C capacity (events per second, disk, one collector per site), the subscriptions (which events), and the D C R (X path for the forwarded log). Exam tip: W E F events land in Windows Event. If detections look for Security Event and find nothing, the data is in the wrong table.

1.title: Checking that data arrives
1.text: Checking that data arrives. Connector status. Connected only when data arrived recently (fourteen days for policy-managed connectors). Table query. Security Event │ take ten or Windows Event │ take ten. Health. The Data collection health monitoring workbook and the Sentinel Health table.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A company must collect Windows security events from servers in an on-premises datacenter with the Windows Security Events via A M A connector. What must be installed first on the servers? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Azure Arc, so that the Azure Monitor Agent can be installed. Machines outside Azure need Azure Arc before the A M A connector can be used.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A sock wants only event I D s four thousand six hundred twenty-four and four thousand six hundred twenty-five from the Security log, to reduce cost. Which collection choice should be selected? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Custom, with an X path query that lists both event I D s. The Custom option collects only the events that match your X path queries.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Security events are forwarded to a W E C server and read by the Windows Forwarded Events connector. In which table do the events land? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Windows Event, the table for forwarded events. Forwarded events go to Windows Event, not Security Event.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. After deploying Windows Forwarded Events, the built-in analytics rules that query Security Event return nothing. What is the fix that keeps the rules unchanged? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Also deploy the Windows Security Events via A M A connector. Built-in rules that query Security Event need the Windows Security Events via A M A connector.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An engineer writes a custom X path query and wants to know which version A M A supports. Which is correct? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: X path one point zero only, validated with Get-Win Event -Filter XPath. A M A supports X path one point zero only; Get-Win Event -Filter XPath validates a query.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. With Windows Event Forwarding, where should the Azure Monitor Agent be installed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: On the Windows Event Collector server that receives the events. A M A is installed on the W E C machine, which reads the forwarded events.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which table does Windows Security Events via A M A write to? Answer: Security Event. Question two. What does a data collection rule define? Answer: What A M A collects, any transformation, and the destination workspace. Question three. What is needed for on-premises machines before A M A? Answer: Azure Arc.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which role creates or edits a D C R? Answer: Monitoring Contributor. Question five. What are the limits for custom X path? Answer: twenty expressions per box, one hundred boxes per rule. Question six. Which collection choices exist besides Custom? Answer: All events, Common and Minimal.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Pattern: connector plus A M A plus D C R; Azure Arc for machines outside Azure. Windows Security Events via A M A: table Security Event; All, Common, Minimal, Custom (X path one point zero). W E F: A M A on the W E C collector; table Windows Event. Roles: Monitoring Contributor for D C Rs; V M Contributor to deploy the agent. Check: Security Event or Windows Event take ten; data collection health workbook.
